certification.name: AWS Certified Generative AI Developer - Professional

domains.name: Foundation Model Integration, Data Management, and Compliance

tasks.name: Implement agentic AI solutions and tool integrations.
Design and implement enterprise integration architectures.
Implement application integration patterns and development tools.

domains.name: Operational Efficiency and Optimization for Generative AI Applications

concepts.name: Build autonomous and multi-agent systems with memory
concepts.description: Design agent systems with appropriate session state, durable memory, multi-agent collaboration, and standardized agent-tool interaction patterns such as MCP.

concepts.name: Implement structured agent reasoning
concepts.description: Use explicit reasoning-and-action loops such as ReAct and controlled orchestration when a problem must be decomposed across multiple steps.

concepts.name: Safeguard autonomous workflows
concepts.description: Use stopping conditions, timeouts, least-privilege IAM, circuit breakers, budgets, and other controls to bound agent behavior.

concepts.name: Coordinate specialized models
concepts.description: Use model selection, specialized FMs, ensembles, or aggregation only when combining capabilities improves the task enough to justify added cost and latency.

concepts.name: Add human collaboration and approval
concepts.description: Use human review, approval, and feedback collection for uncertain, sensitive, or high-impact agent decisions.

concepts.name: Implement reliable agent tools
concepts.description: Define tool schemas and behaviors clearly, validate parameters, handle errors, and scope permissions so tool calls are reliable and safe.

concepts.name: Host and consume MCP tool servers
concepts.description: Use Lambda for lightweight stateless MCP servers or ECS/containers for more complex and long-lived tool services, with consistent MCP clients.

concepts.name: Choose an inference deployment mode
concepts.description: Match serverless/on-demand, Provisioned Throughput, or SageMaker endpoint deployment to traffic, customization, latency, and cost needs.

concepts.name: Size LLM serving infrastructure
concepts.description: Account for GPU/accelerator memory, model size, token processing, batching, and concurrency when hosting models yourself.

concepts.name: Cascade models for cost and latency
concepts.description: Route easy tasks to smaller models and escalate only when confidence, complexity, or policy requires a stronger model.

concepts.name: Connect FMs to enterprise environments
concepts.description: Use APIs, event-driven integration, and synchronization patterns to connect GenAI capabilities with legacy and enterprise systems while controlling coupling.

concepts.name: Enhance existing applications with GenAI
concepts.description: Use API Gateway, Lambda, EventBridge, and microservice/webhook patterns to add FM capabilities to existing business applications.

concepts.name: Federate identity and enforce least privilege
concepts.description: Use identity federation, RBAC, and least-privilege API/model/data permissions so enterprise identities receive only authorized GenAI capabilities.

concepts.name: Design hybrid and edge GenAI integrations
concepts.description: Use Outposts, Wavelength, and secure hybrid routing when data locality, jurisdiction, or edge-latency requirements constrain where processing occurs.

concepts.name: Build GenAI CI/CD and gateway architectures
concepts.description: Automate code/prompt/config tests, security scans, evaluation gates, deployment and rollback, and centralize model access with a governed abstraction or gateway.

concepts.name: Invoke FMs synchronously and asynchronously
concepts.description: Use direct Bedrock APIs for interactive calls and queues/workflows for long-running or decoupled processing.

concepts.name: Stream model responses
concepts.description: Use ConverseStream or other streaming response patterns with WebSockets, SSE, or chunked transfer to reduce perceived latency.

concepts.name: Handle throttling and transient API failures
concepts.description: Use exponential backoff, jitter, rate limiting, retries, fallback, and tracing for reliable model calls.

concepts.name: Route requests to the right model
concepts.description: Use static, rules-based, or intelligent routing based on modality, complexity, tenant, latency, cost, and quality requirements.

concepts.name: Integrate GenAI with application APIs
concepts.description: Handle request validation, streaming, timeouts, quotas, and retry behavior at API boundaries.

concepts.name: Build front-end and workflow integrations
concepts.description: Use Amplify, OpenAPI-based clients, Prompt Flows, and AWS serverless services to connect user experiences to GenAI workflows.

concepts.name: Automate document and workflow processing
concepts.description: Use Lambda, Step Functions, and Bedrock Data Automation or related services to coordinate extraction and generative processing.

concepts.name: Use Amazon Q Developer in development workflows
concepts.description: Use Q Developer for coding assistance, explanation, troubleshooting, and productivity while keeping normal review and security practices.

concepts.name: Compose agent and workflow frameworks
concepts.description: Choose Strands, Agent Squad, Step Functions, or prompt chaining based on autonomy, control, and orchestration needs.

concepts.name: Trace application failures across services
concepts.description: Use CloudWatch Logs Insights, X-Ray, traces, and developer tooling to correlate model, API, Lambda, and downstream failures.
